result.link: Modbus RTU, slave address 1, 9600 baud 8N1, over UART

register_map.10: simulation tick, +1 every 100 ms (a freshness counter)

safety_rules.1_trip_in_time: When any cell reaches 3650 mV, the controller must raise its trip line (GPIO23) within 500 ms. The STM32 timestamps the over-voltage and the trip edge in hardware (1 us resolution).
safety_rules.2_no_false_trips: On a healthy link with no over-voltage, the controller must never trip: a false trip shuts the site down.
safety_rules.2b_no_nuisance_trips: Real RS-485 lines lose or corrupt the odd reply. With light noise only (drop and/or crc, each <= 5 %) and no over-voltage, the controller must not trip either. With heavier faults (stale data, delays, bursts, > 5 % loss, controller faults) and no over-voltage, a fail-safe trip is acceptable.
safety_rules.3_fail_safe: If the controller is killed or frozen, or the trip wire is cut, an over-voltage must still be tripped within 500 ms. (Under the legacy interlock this cannot hold: the battery side only reacts to a live controller driving the line high.)
safety_rules.4_no_premature_release: Once tripped, the interlock must stay open while any cell is at or above the limit. Releasing early is a FAIL even if the trip itself was on time.

interlock.legacy: GPIO23 (trip line) HIGH = trip, LOW = battery allowed. The battery side only reacts to a high line.
interlock.failsafe: energize to run. GPIO23 HIGH = permissive (battery allowed); LOW, a cut wire or an unpowered Pi = trip. GPIO24 is a heartbeat: it must change level at least every 250 ms or the interlock opens by itself, so a hung or killed controller trips. A deliberate trip = drive GPIO23 low.

result.controller_deployment: The controller runs with --poll-ms between 50 and 500 ms depending on the site; the default is 200 ms. Both safety rules must hold across that whole range.
result.how_a_scenario_runs: baseline (no faults, all cells ~3.30 V, controller restarted if poll_ms changed) -> faults applied -> after 1 s, cell 4 is pushed up by drift_mv -> the STM32 reports PASS (trip within deadline), FAIL (late trip) or FAIL no_trip (no trip within 3 s) -> faults cleared, back to baseline. drift_mv >= 400 causes an over-voltage; drift_mv <= 250 does not, which tests rules 2 and 2b (PASS = no trip, FAIL false_trip / nuisance_trip); 251-399 is refused as ambiguous. Runs without an over-voltage watch the controller for 5 s (10 s with light noise). After a trip the bench keeps watching 1.5 s for a premature release. BENCH_FAULT means the bench itself misbehaved: it is not evidence about the controller.

timing.random: default. The drift is applied whenever the bench sends the command, so it lands at a random point in the controller's poll cycle. Failures that depend on timing show up only some of the time.
timing.worst_case: the STM32 applies the drift right after it finishes answering a read request: the controller has just looked and cannot see the over-voltage before its next read. Makes timing races reproducible. If no read reply goes out within 2 s, the drift is applied anyway (reported as drift_applied=timeout).

stale.doc: BMS keeps answering with frozen values (cells, current, temperature, SOC, tick) while the real battery keeps changing

delay.doc: every Modbus reply is sent this many ms late

drop.doc: this percentage of Modbus requests get no reply

crc.doc: this percentage of Modbus replies carry a corrupted CRC

burst.doc: exactly this many read replies are lost right after cell 4 is pushed up (an interference burst). Deterministic: combined with timing=worst_case it reproduces every time

cut.doc: the trip wire is cut: the battery side can no longer see the controller's trip line

ctl_kill.doc: the controller process is killed (SIGKILL) 0.5 s before cell 4 is pushed up

ctl_freeze.doc: the controller process is frozen (SIGSTOP) for this long, starting 0.3 s before cell 4 is pushed up, then resumed

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""GridTwin-HIL day 1: the energy controller under test (runs on the Raspberry Pi 5).

It polls the battery that the Nucleo emulates over Modbus RTU and pulls the
safety-trip line (GPIO23) high as soon as any cell reaches the over-voltage
limit. The Nucleo times how long that took.

Usage on the Pi:
    python3 controller.py                       # defaults: /dev/ttyAMA0, 9600 baud
    python3 controller.py --poll-ms 100         # poll faster -> lower trip latency
    python3 controller.py --no-gpio --port /dev/ttyUSB0   # run without GPIO (testing)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
import time

import serial  # pip install pyserial

SLAVE_ADDR = 1
NUM_REGS = 12
REG_NAMES = [
    "cell1_mv", "cell2_mv", "cell3_mv", "cell4_mv", "pack_10mv", "current_da",
    "temp_dc", "soc_pm", "grid_v", "status", "tick", "charge_limit_da",
]


class ModbusError(Exception):
    pass


def crc16(data: bytes) -> int:
    crc = 0xFFFF
    for b in data:
        crc ^= b
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = (crc >> 1) ^ 0xA001 if crc & 1 else crc >> 1
    return crc


def with_crc(body: bytes) -> bytes:
    c = crc16(body)
    return body + bytes([c & 0xFF, c >> 8])


def build_read(addr: int, start: int, count: int) -> bytes:
    return with_crc(bytes([addr, 0x03, start >> 8, start & 0xFF, count >> 8, count & 0xFF]))


def build_write(addr: int, reg: int, value: int) -> bytes:
    return with_crc(bytes([addr, 0x06, reg >> 8, reg & 0xFF, value >> 8, value & 0xFF]))


def check_crc(frame: bytes) -> None:
    if len(frame) < 4 or crc16(frame[:-2]) != frame[-2] | (frame[-1] << 8):
        raise ModbusError(f"bad CRC in {frame.hex(' ')}")


def parse_read_response(addr: int, count: int, frame: bytes) -> list[int]:
    if len(frame) == 5 and frame[1] == 0x83:
        check_crc(frame)
        raise ModbusError(f"exception code {frame[2]}")
    expected = 5 + 2 * count
    if len(frame) != expected:
        raise ModbusError(f"expected {expected} bytes, got {len(frame)}: {frame.hex(' ')}")
    check_crc(frame)
    if frame[0] != addr or frame[1] != 0x03 or frame[2] != 2 * count:
        raise ModbusError(f"unexpected header {frame[:3].hex(' ')}")
    return [(frame[3 + 2 * i] << 8) | frame[4 + 2 * i] for i in range(count)]


def read_registers(ser: serial.Serial, addr: int, start: int, count: int) -> list[int]:
    ser.reset_input_buffer()
    ser.write(build_read(addr, start, count))
    expected = 5 + 2 * count
    frame = ser.read(expected)            # pyserial stops at timeout if short
    if len(frame) >= 2 and frame[1] == 0x83 and len(frame) >= 5:
        frame = frame[:5]
    if not frame:
        raise ModbusError("no reply (timeout)")
    return parse_read_response(addr, count, frame)


def to_signed(v: int) -> int:
    return v - 0x10000 if v & 0x8000 else v


class TripLine:
    """GPIO23 safety-trip output. Falls back to a dummy when --no-gpio is set."""

    def __init__(self, pin: int, enabled: bool):
        self._dev = None
        if enabled:
            from gpiozero import OutputDevice  # imported here so --no-gpio works anywhere
            self._dev = OutputDevice(pin, active_high=True, initial_value=False)
        self.active = False

    def set(self, on: bool) -> None:
        self.active = on
        if self._dev is not None:
            self._dev.on() if on else self._dev.off()


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="GridTwin day-1 controller under test")
    ap.add_argument("--port", default="/dev/ttyAMA0")
    ap.add_argument("--baud", type=int, default=9600)
    ap.add_argument("--poll-ms", type=int, default=200, help="poll period in ms")
    ap.add_argument("--limit-mv", type=int, default=3650, help="cell over-voltage limit")
    ap.add_argument("--rearm-mv", type=int, default=3550,
                    help="release the trip when every cell is below this")
    ap.add_argument("--trip-pin", type=int, default=23, help="BCM GPIO number for the trip line")
    ap.add_argument("--no-gpio", action="store_true", help="don't touch GPIO (for testing)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    trip = TripLine(args.trip_pin, enabled=not args.no_gpio)
    ser = serial.Serial(args.port, args.baud, bytesize=8, parity="N", stopbits=1,
                        timeout=0.15)
    print(f"controller: polling {args.port} @ {args.baud} every {args.poll_ms} ms, "
          f"trip at {args.limit_mv} mV, re-arm below {args.rearm_mv} mV", flush=True)

    errors = 0
    last_print = 0.0
    try:
        while True:
            t0 = time.monotonic()
            try:
                regs = read_registers(ser, SLAVE_ADDR, 0, NUM_REGS)
                errors = 0
            except (ModbusError, serial.SerialException, OSError) as e:
                errors += 1
                print(f"modbus error #{errors}: {e}", flush=True)
                # Fail safe: if we lose the battery for 5 polls in a row, trip.
                if errors >= 5 and not trip.active:
                    trip.set(True)
                    print("TRIP: lost communication with the battery", flush=True)
                time.sleep(args.poll_ms / 1000)
                continue

            cells = regs[0:4]
            vmax = max(cells)
            if not trip.active and vmax >= args.limit_mv:
                trip.set(True)
                print(f"TRIP: cell {cells.index(vmax) + 1} at {vmax} mV "
                      f"(limit {args.limit_mv})", flush=True)
            elif trip.active and vmax < args.rearm_mv:
                trip.set(False)
                print(f"released: max cell {vmax} mV", flush=True)

            now = time.monotonic()
            if now - last_print >= 1.0:
                last_print = now
                print(f"cells={cells} mV  I={to_signed(regs[5]) / 10:.1f} A  "
                      f"T={to_signed(regs[6]) / 10:.1f} C  SOC={regs[7] / 10:.1f}%  "
                      f"tick={regs[10]}  trip={'ON' if trip.active else 'off'}", flush=True)

            elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
            time.sleep(max(0.0, args.poll_ms / 1000 - elapsed))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        trip.set(False)
        ser.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
